title: ClickHouse chaos: kill a shard replica; Distributed query reroutes
description: The nexus-cli chaos verb for the analytics tier: kill clickhouse-server on one replica of shard 2 and verify a Distributed SELECT still returns shard 2's rows from the surviving replica (no data unavailability with replication_num/2-per-shard), then auto-recover on restart (the replica catches up via Keeper).

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.44 "clickhouse-client --secure --host localhost --port 9440 --query 'SELECT count() FROM nexus.events'"

observe.what: (silent) shard2-rep1 is down; shard2-rep2 (192.168.70.47) still serves shard 2

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.44 "clickhouse-client --secure --host localhost --port 9440 --query 'SELECT count() FROM nexus.events SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards=0'"

observe.what: still 600 -- the Distributed query reroutes shard 2 to its surviving replica (shard2-rep2); no rows lost (replication tolerates 1 replica loss per shard, ADR-0029)

observe.where: ssh nexusadmin@192.168.70.46 "clickhouse-client --secure --host localhost --port 9440 --query 'SELECT is_readonly, absolute_delay FROM system.replicas'"
observe.what: recovered replica rejoins (is_readonly=0) and catches up via Keeper (absolute_delay returns to ~0)

whatProves: killing one replica of a shard does not make that shard's data unavailable -- the Distributed query reroutes to the surviving replica (2 replicas per shard) -- and the replica auto-recovers + re-syncs via Keeper on restart. Replication is real, not cosmetic.
